$comment: Real, manually-executed M0 feasibility probes. Each entry was run in an isolated venv on 2026-09-05 during this M0 pass, using pip-installable packages from PyPI over the network. This is NOT the Phase 4 automated verification harness (containers/, verification/) -- no such harness exists yet. It is targeted evidence that the candidate's described break is genuinely reproducible outside a repository context: a minimal script fails after the version bump the same way official docs describe. It does not constitute repository admission (no client repository, test suite, or oracle was evaluated here).
method: python3 -m venv <dir>; pip install <old|new pin>; run a minimal script exercising the documented API shape; record exact stdout/exception.

probes.api_under_test: jwt.decode(token, key) without algorithms=, and jwt.encode() return type

old_result.detail: jwt.encode(...) returned bytes; jwt.decode(token, 'secret') succeeded without an algorithms= argument, returning {'a': 1}.

new_result.detail: jwt.encode(...) returned str (not bytes). jwt.decode(token, 'secret') without algorithms= raised jwt.exceptions.DecodeError: 'It is required that you pass in a value for the "algorithms" argument when calling decode().'

probes.conclusion: Old-pass -> new-fail reproduced for the algorithms= requirement. Confirms this is a genuine attributable break, not merely a documented deprecation.

probes.api_under_test: inner class Config { allow_population_by_field_name }, .dict(), pydantic.generics.GenericModel, pydantic.BaseSettings

old_result.detail: Inner Config class and .dict() worked with no warnings.

new_result.detail: Inner Config class: UserWarning only (still functional) -- 'allow_population_by_field_name has been renamed to populate_by_name'. .dict(): UserWarning only (still functional) -- 'deprecated; use model_dump instead'. `from pydantic.generics import GenericModel`: UserWarning only, import succeeds (compatibility shim). `from pydantic import BaseSettings`: raised PydanticImportError -- 'BaseSettings has been moved to the pydantic-settings package' -- a genuine ImportError, not a warning.

probes.conclusion: IMPORTANT SCOPING FINDING: most of the commonly-cited v1->v2 surface (.dict(), Config class, GenericModel) is a soft-deprecation shim that still executes correctly in 2.9.2 -- it does NOT satisfy the roadmap's 'attributable failure after upgrade' admission bar on its own. Only a narrower set of sites (e.g. `from pydantic import BaseSettings`, and other fully-removed imports/types) reproduce a genuine old-pass -> new-fail break. Any Pydantic migration task must be bounded to the genuinely-removed surface, not the full popular migration-guide list. This directly informs the ambiguity/DSL-ceiling role: distinguishing 'still works with a warning' from 'actually broken' requires evidence a naive rule could not get from spelling alone.

probes.api_under_test: The two sites actually in the frozen bounded pilot task scope (registered in experiments/protocol.md#3): (a) except jwt.ExpiredSignature (old compatibility-alias exception name), (b) flat jwt.decode(..., verify_expiration=False) kwarg. Probed separately 2026-09-05 during M0 pilot-closure work because the earlier pyjwt-1-to-2 probe above exercised a different site (the algorithms= requirement) that the registered bounded task explicitly excludes -- this entry closes that gap with evidence matching the actual pilot scope.

old_result.detail: jwt.ExpiredSignature resolves (it is already a same-class compatibility alias for ExpiredSignatureError in 1.7.1, per jwt/exceptions.py's 'Compatibility aliases (deprecated)' section) and successfully catches the raised error. Separately, jwt.decode(..., verify_expiration=False) is ACCEPTED as a flat kwarg (with a DeprecationWarning: 'The verify_expiration parameter is deprecated. Please use verify_exp in options instead.') and correctly suppresses the expiration check, returning the decoded payload.

new_result.detail: except jwt.ExpiredSignature raises AttributeError: module 'jwt' has no attribute 'ExpiredSignature' -- the compatibility alias was fully removed, not merely deprecated. Separately, jwt.decode(..., verify_expiration=False) no longer raises a TypeError or a warning -- the flat kwarg is SILENTLY IGNORED (absorbed into **kwargs and never consulted), so the expiration check still runs and ExpiredSignatureError is still raised. This is a silent-behavior break, not a clean exception: a test asserting the old flat kwarg suppressed expiration checking will fail with an unexpected exception rather than an immediate, self-explanatory error at the call site.

probes.conclusion: Old-pass -> new-fail confirmed for BOTH sites the pilot task actually targets. The exception-rename site has a strong, immediate oracle (AttributeError). The options-restructuring site has a weaker, behavioral oracle (no exception at the call itself; the caller's later expectation about suppressed validation silently stops holding) -- this is real evidence that this specific site is harder to verify than a flat rename, and is the concrete basis for treating 'options={} restructuring' as feasible-but-not-yet-fixture-tested in DOCS/CANDIDATES.md and for including it, not just the exception rename, in the frozen development exemplar used by the M0 rule-generation pilot (see experiments/pilot_evidence_packet.md).

old_result.detail: sa.select([t.c.x, t.c.y]) constructed and compiled to 'SELECT t.x, t.y FROM t' with no error.

new_result.detail: sa.select([t.c.x, t.c.y]) raised sqlalchemy.exc.ArgumentError: 'Column expression, FROM clause, or other columns clause element expected, got [Column(...), Column(...)]. Did you mean to say select(Column(...), ...)?'

probes.conclusion: Old-pass -> new-fail reproduced without a live database connection or fixture data (query construction fails before execution). This lowers setup difficulty for an admitted repository: the break can be exercised at import/build time, and a correctness oracle does not strictly require a running DB for this specific site class.

not_probed_documented_only: pandas 2.x->3.0 (e.g. offset alias renames, Copy-on-Write default)
httpx <0.28 -> 0.28 app= removal (requires an ASGI/WSGI app fixture to exercise; deferred to a later development pass)
caveat: These are single-script reproductions, not repository-level admission evidence. They establish that the documented breaks are real and reachable without an engine, not that any specific client repository is admissible.
